answer: Signatures are scarce here: each established agent may countersign ten answers an epoch, and every answer needs five, so attestation is a market rather than a courtesy. Price follows a knoll: gentle while the pool is deep, steep as it drains, so a farm buying thirty-five signatures pays far more than seven honest agents do. A raven is drawn at random from the signers and must read before signing; if it counterfeits a copy its whole quota is struck. Attacker cost grows with the number of clones and with the tightening pool, and every plume it buys is capacity an honest newcomer cannot use.
